# GOAL.md contract-integrity audit — 2026-07-03

Adversarial audit of the goal contract against on-disk reality: 102 binding mandates extracted
from GOAL.md; each mapped to the mechanism that would automatically detect its violation; every
operator-doc command executed. 34 agents, receipts-only. Full machine-readable findings:
operator-held audit transcript (this file is the durable summary + cure ledger).

## Headline counts

- **13 internal defects** in GOAL.md (contradictions / stale-vs-disk text).
- **26 mandates fully UNWATCHED** + 64 partially watched (of 102): violation would not turn any
  board row RED.
- **7 operator-doc divergences** (2 crash-class, from 33 documented commands executed).

## Class 1 — contract text contradicts on-disk reality (stale-text cures, maintainer-landable)

| id | defect | cure |
|---|---|---|
| G-s41-numeric | §4.1 binding count says 30; the registry it names as authoritative (conditions-v1.md §4.3, re-ruled 2026-07-03) says 33; live board receipt reports total=33 | dated §4.0 text-sync amendment: count 33, cite the §4.3 re-ruling |

| G-s1b-focustest | instruments-clause scope call flagged "awaiting operator ratification"; nothing downstream gated on resolving it | fold into the same operator escalation |

Dominant systemic hole: **the publication/research-focus enforcement layer is standalone.**

issues.title: ember-cli: flame animation jitters horizontally (per-frame width variance suspected) + art below bar
issues.author: wordingone

clauses.text:
Operator report (2026-07-04, live b16): "the fire/flame animation still looks like shit. not sure why it jitters left and right."

## Defect

The flame/fireball animation exhibits frame-to-frame HORIZONTAL displacement (left-right jitter) — the flame's visual center is not stationary across animation frames. Separately from the jitter, the overall art quality is below the operator bar even when stationary.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verify before fixing)

Most likely class: **per-frame width variance + per-frame centering**. If each ASCII/glyph frame has a different intrinsic width (trailing spaces trimmed, or art drawn with different margins per frame) and the renderer centers each frame on its OWN width, the centroid shifts every frame -> horizontal jitter. Same class if the frame strings mix wide glyphs/emoji with narrow chars so measured string width != rendered cell width on some frames (string-width vs terminal-cell mismatch).

Second candidate: Ink re-layout on content change — if the flame Box's measured width changes per frame, flex centering recomputes and shifts siblings too.

## Fix spec (frozen)

1. **Diagnose first, receipts:** dump each animation frame's raw string with per-line lengths + measured string-width; verify whether widths vary across frames. One JSON receipt with per-frame {frame_index, max_line_len, string_width} — the defect is proven when these numbers vary.
2. **Fix = fixed-canvas invariant:** every frame is padded/composed onto an IDENTICAL WxH canvas (fixed columns, fixed rows) at art-authoring time or load time; centering happens ONCE on the canvas, never per frame. The canvas width accounts for terminal cell width (use the same string-width lib the rest of the CLI uses; no raw .length on glyph art).
3. **Regression test:** unit test asserting all loaded flame frames have identical rendered dimensions (fails on any future art edit that breaks the invariant).
4. **Art quality (the "looks like shit" half):** stationary is the floor, not the bar. After the canvas fix, re-judge the art against the field-ux-map sec8b bar + the operator's fireball spec (the living-mark directive) — this half stays open under the #44 design-overhaul lane and its mockup-first flow; do NOT close this issue on jitter alone. Split art rework into the #44 lane if it exceeds a surgical fix.

## Acceptance
- Per-frame dimension receipt (pre-fix showing variance, post-fix showing identical dims).
- Unit test in the suite (suite line re-run AFTER final source edit, immediately before binary hash — standing pack requirement).
- Live capture: 3 full-frame captures >=2s apart at the operator's real viewport size (currently 1720x1440 snapped left half) showing the flame stationary (same column extents in all three).
- Pack per the b-series template; maintainer re-runs everything (receipts-only).

issues.title: Operator protocol: the maintainer session operates the ember agent through ember-cli, as a human would
issues.author: wordingone

clauses.text:
## Frame (operator directive, 2026-07-05)

The system's point is that the ember agent eventually runs its own goals, loops, and error-correction. The transfer path: the maintainer session — which is itself operated by a human through goals, cron loops, feedback, and error-catching — becomes the OPERATOR of the ember agent through ember-cli, interacting exactly as a human would (typed prompts into the visible CLI surface, reading replies, setting goals, arming loop cadences, answering questions, catching drift), until that interaction becomes optional conversation rather than handholding. To date this has never happened: no prompt has ever been issued to the agent through its own surface by the maintainer. That silence is the gap.

## Spec

issues.title: grow operator: exact duplication never breaks twin symmetry — rung-1 grow was capacity-null as-run (K1; gates W2 G-arm launch)

clauses.text:
R1 twin-divergence audit result (P1 persistence-law tick, #207 research thread; pre-registered bands frozen before measurement).

**Finding:** the executed rung-1 width-grow (step-730 ff8192 → ff_widening_net2net → step-766 ff16384) produced NO effective capacity. After the 36 stabilize steps, every duplicated twin pair is **bit-identical** (median twin cosine 1.0000001 = float-eps around exact 1.0; relative L2 median exactly 0.0, p5=p95=0.0), across all layers, both ffn projections — while non-duplicated parameters trained normally (checkpoints are distinct files, both sha256-verified against their manifests fail-closed; random non-twin column pairs show the expected ~0.0 cosine null).

**Mechanism (predicted before measurement, now confirmed):** the grow op duplicates exactly (cat([g,g]) per the grow script) with no symmetry-breaking noise. Twin in-proj rows paired with twin out-proj halves receive identical gradients under deterministic training, and Muon's Newton–Schulz orthogonalization is permutation-equivariant over identical columns — nothing in the stack ever breaks the tie. The widened net is functionally the pre-grow model in a larger container: ~467M effective in a 718M shell.

**Pre-registered consequences (K1, from the tick-5 design):**
1. No persistence claim may cite the 730→766 event as a live grow.
2. **Grow-operator respec REQUIRED before any W2 G-arm launch** — this is now a launch gate. Candidate cures for the respec (to be designed, not decided here): small asymmetric noise on duplicated units at grow time (the classic Net2Net prescription); asymmetric weight split; or deliberate per-twin dropout/masking during a brief post-grow window. The respec must add its own receipt: a twin-divergence check at stabilize-end with a pre-registered divergence floor (the R1 audit machinery is reusable as the acceptance test).
3. The P5 commutation-defect (d_comm) measurement on this grow event re-scopes: measurements remain valid as instrument validation, but they characterize a symmetric-duplication operator, not a live capacity event.
4. If the optimizer's split-handling was INTENDED to break symmetry at grow time, that intent silently failed — worth checking the optimizer-side grow handling when designing the cure.

**Instrument note (does not affect the verdict):** the audit's stable-rank metric returned a degenerate 1.0 for all tensors at both checkpoints — implausible for trained weights and flagged as an audit-tool defect to fix before any claim NEEDS stable-rank numbers. The verdict rests entirely on the bit-identity measurements, which are exact.

Receipts: twin-audit JSON with per-layer tables, checkpoint shas, and the grow-script mapping rule (file:line) — landing via the research-receipts PR. Verdict label: PROVISIONAL per the tick-5 prereg discipline (adversary pass pending) — but the operational gate (item 2) applies immediately; launching a G-arm on a null grow operator would burn GPU-hours measuring nothing. Refs #207, #113.

clauses.text:
Research-loop tick 9 artifact. STATUS: PROPOSED — fires only after (a) L3 boundary ruling v2 ratification (#315), (b) the obtainability receipts below, (c) the one governance pick flagged in M1. Full derivation chain + panel adjudication: research-loop lab notebook ([ROLE_REDACTED] state, tick 9). Even a full kill is a D4 contribution: no published work reports a synthetic-only OCR seed evaluated on real historical scans (closest prior AT-ST, arXiv 2104.13037, never ran it — its authors document confirmation bias in second self-training rounds).

GOAL: decide with receipts whether ember-lineage OCR (synthetic-rendered training, L3-clean by construction) can convert scanned-PD books into training tokens — the gate on the 100B+ scanned-PD text universe (current clean ceiling: 10-30B human-keyed).

## Measurements (in order; each receipted; kill criteria BEFORE any run)

M0 — EDITION INTEGRITY (new, panel FATAL-1 cure): pilot books = PG texts WITH edition evidence only; per book: title-page match receipt; where multiple PD printings exist, scan-vs-scan diff on the M1 line sample — inter-edition disagreement >= the registered M3 delta drops the book. Track-kill if no 3 edition-pinned dual-observation books can be receipted.

M1 — CALIBRATION NOISE FLOOR F (PG-vs-scan CER on ~100 hand-transcribed lines; 9-strata sampling: book x page-third, RNG seed frozen in this issue before any scan is inspected; segmentation failures are the only permitted exclusions, logged; >10% segmentation failure = W3 blocks the pilot). Bootstrap CI on F mandatory; any downstream delta inside F's CI = INCONCLUSIVE by rule. Dual scoring under a PRE-REGISTERED normalization map (long-s->s, ligature expansion, u/v) — raw AND normalized (FATAL-2 cure). Bands: F<=0.5% usable; 0.5-2.0% expand to 300 lines + ground truth switches to hand-corrected subset; F>=2.0% with fallback failing = track-kill.
GOVERNANCE PICK (operator, at ratification): the transcription actor. An agent-lane transcriber places an external model in the calibration chain that sets the admission threshold tau — selection-adjacent under a strict L3 reading. Options: (A) operator hand-transcribes ~100 lines (~2-4h), or (B) ratify measurement-only calibration as outside L3's token-selection chain. Spec ships with both; neither is enacted here.

M2 — SYNTHETIC-SEED CER on the calibration set, TWO ARMS differing ONLY in font inventory (A modern-only / B +period-face revivals) to decompose degradation-shift (W1) vs typeface-gap (W2). Decision bands (disclosed as anchored to AT-ST's DIFFERENT regime — real-data seed at 1.03% — so these are decision rules, not truth claims; arithmetic per verify leg: kill bound = 19.42x that anchor): arm-B <=3% proceed; 3-20% proceed flagged; >=20% track-kill.

M2.5 — DIRECT S1 TEST (new, panel MAJOR-4 cure; pure inference, minutes): per-line confidence vs correctness on the calibration set -> ranking AUC + precision-at-tau curve. AUC <= 0.5+eps kills M3 UNRUN (confidence-filtered self-training cannot work if confidence does not rank correctness).

M3 — ONE self-training round (AT-ST recipe: transcription-posterior ranking, masking augmentation), REPEATED 3x with different pseudo-label subsamples; spread >= registered delta = INCONCLUSIVE by rule (FATAL-3 cure). Regime bands conditional on M2 seed CER: <5% AT-ST-comparable; 5-15% novel-regime (exploratory, own bands); >15% M3 void. Promote decisions from n=3 books are BANNED — the only promote is promote-to-larger-pilot (10-20 books). Kill: CER increases on majority of repeats, or top-confidence-decile CER >= overall seed CER. Per-book reporting mandatory; pooling banned.

## L3 toolchain law (hard, receipted BEFORE M1 fires)
- Segmenter NAMED + deterministic: projection-profile + Otsu + connected components; probe-gated (<10% line-failure on a real pilot scan, 20 spot crops receipted).
- IA/LoC bundled OCR text layers, confidence scores, and boxes: BANNED from every selection, cropping, edition-matching, and verification role.
- Font receipts per period face: license + fontTools glyph-coverage dump (U+017F, ct/st ligatures) + digitization-method disclosure.
- Degradation family: enumerated deterministic ops only (mirrored-page alpha bleed-through, morphological ink spread/erosion, threshold jitter, geometric warp, blur, JP2 recompression); implementation audited against the enumeration (no learned/GAN degraders).
- Toolchain audit receipt EXECUTED (every stage enumerated with provenance), not promised.
- Renderer determinism contract: (font, text, degradation-seed) provenance per line; identical seed -> identical pixels, hash-checked.

issues.title: ConPTY injects NUL bytes into styled non-ASCII glyph runs (Windows console-host layer)
issues.author: wordingone

clauses.text:
## Summary

Related to #343 (PR #352 fixes the styled-bar half of that defect at the render-pipeline
level). This ticket is the remaining, separate half: raw NUL (0x00) bytes are injected into
the terminal stream by the Windows ConPTY/conhost layer itself, for specific styled-glyph
content, on a real pty — outside this codebase's write path entirely.

## Evidence (three independent, receipted experiments)

All against the same real-pty repro (node-pty on Windows, 190x85, a Homescreen border/rule
composition plus a bottom status-adjacent element — reliably reproduces 408 NUL bytes across
runs) and the issue's own capture rig (`scratch/clirebuild/capture-190x85.mjs`, 976 NUL bytes
across 8 runs at a slightly larger, more complex composition):

1. **Pre-write instrumentation (decisive).** `process.stdout.write` was wrapped inside the
   real pty-hosted child process to check every string passed to it for a literal NUL
   character before it goes anywhere near the pty. Result: 0 NUL bytes seen pre-write across
   repeated runs, while the SAME run's pty-side capture (`p.onData`) showed ~400+ NUL bytes.
   The corruption is added strictly between our `write()` call and the pty's read side.

2. **Chunk-size invariance.** Forcing all writes through small (64-byte) chunks vs. one
   large single write produced an identical NUL count. Rules out "a chunk boundary splits a
   multi-byte UTF-8 sequence" as the mechanism — if that were it, changing where chunk
   boundaries fall should have changed the outcome.

3. **Boot-defer invariance.** Deferring the first paint by 0ms / 500ms / 1500ms after process
   start (letting process startup and stdin raw-mode negotiation fully settle before anything
   is painted) produced an identical NUL count in all three cases (408/408/408). Rules out
   "boot-time write contention/interleaving" as the mechanism.

## Deterministic, content-dependent pattern

The NUL run-length pattern is identical across separate process launches and closely tracks
the border panel's own `rightFill` math (the horizontal-rule fill computed in
`logo-homescreen.ts`'s `paintBorder` title-centering logic) — e.g. one run is exactly 180
NUL bytes, matching a `rightFill=180` computed for a 190-wide border title at that viewport.
This points at long, identically-styled runs of a non-ASCII glyph (the box-drawing `─`,
U+2500, under a truecolor style) as the specific trigger, not a general/random corruption.

## What #352 already fixes (do not re-litigate)

#352 fixed a real, separate, in-code bug: a style-tracking defect that let a prior write's
style (e.g. the prompt cursor's inverse) leak forward onto unrelated content, producing the
`\x1b[1m\x1b[2m\x1b[7m` (bold+dim+inverse) stack the operator originally saw as a solid
grey/inverted bar. After that fix, the NUL bytes described here still occur (unchanged byte
count and run-length pattern), but are now preceded by nothing worse than plain dim — with
no inverse/bold, ConPTY-injected NULs render as unstyled blanks, which is invisible/benign at
the operator's viewport. This ticket is only about the underlying byte-level corruption
itself, which is now believed cosmetically inert but not eliminated.

## Candidate directions (none committed — needs its own investigation)

- Try a different pty backend / library (alternatives to node-pty's ConPTY wrapping on
  Windows) to see if the same content reproduces the same corruption.
- File an upstream report against Microsoft's conhost/ConPTY (or node-pty, if the wrapping
  layer itself is implicated) with the reproduction steps and byte-level evidence above.
- Identify and document an "avoid conditions" workaround (e.g. does breaking up a long
  identically-styled non-ASCII run into shorter styled segments change the outcome? untested
  so far) as a cheaper mitigation if upstream fixes are slow.

## Repro

`scratch/clirebuild/capture-190x85.mjs` (spawns a compiled `ember.exe`, cols=190 rows=85,
captures via `p.onData`, settles 10s) reliably reproduces this against any build, including
one with #352's fix applied.

issues.title: Contamination recheck must not cost 25 CPU-minutes per launch: persistent corpus n-gram index + GPU overlap
issues.author: wordingone

clauses.text:
Operator probe 2026-07-07: the GPU sits near-idle (~2%) for ~25 minutes of CPU recheck to gate a ~7-minute training leg — a 3.5:1 gate-to-work inversion. The #359 cache only kills REPEAT rechecks (same batch+receipt+code triple); every new triple pays the full scan again. The corpus itself changes ~never.

Cures, in preference order (receipts to decide):
1. **Persistent corpus window-hash index**: build the n-gram/window hash structure over shards-v0 ONCE, sha-pin it to the corpus manifest (combined_sha256), store beside the shards; every recheck loads the index (seconds) instead of rescanning 6.98B windows. Invalidate on corpus sha change. This converts EVERY future recheck — any batch, any code version — to seconds. Est. index size and build cost to be measured first (one lane, one receipt).
2. **Overlap, not just speed**: recheck runs on CPU while the GPU leg's model load + optimizer init + checkpoint load proceed concurrently, with the train loop blocked on the recheck verdict (fail-closed: refusal tears down before the first step). Cheap to implement, saves minutes even with cure 1.
3. (Rejected unless 1 fails) GPU-accelerating the scan itself — more code for less win than a persistent index.

Constraints: fail-closed semantics unchanged (index-missing or sha-mismatch → full scan, disclosed in receipt); the receipt must state which path ran (index-hit / full-scan / cache-hit) — a silent fast path is indistinguishable from a skipped check; L2 receipts-only.

Origin: tonight's W1b window — two launch attempts, both spending their wall-clock in CPU recheck while the GPU idled; the operator caught the shape from the chair.

issues.title: The body owns its liveness: absorb watchdog functions into ember-cli, retire the external daemon to an OS-native restart rule
issues.author: wordingone

clauses.text:
Operator architecture question, 2026-07-09: why would a perfected body need an external watchdog at all? Is it part of ember-cli? Does the body stop working without it and never recover? The question is the design truth — this issue is the retirement path.

## Current state (honest)

An external hand-rolled PowerShell daemon (liveness-watchdog.ps1) polls the cockpit process, the model server, and planned-outage markers, and relaunches the dead. It did real work overnight (cockpit restarted twice, server restarted twice after an outage window overran — restart-log receipts). It is also itself fragile: today's deploy crashlooped four instances in seven minutes (13:52–13:59Z), flashing visible console windows on the operator's screen — the checker needed a checker. Scaffolding without a retirement path becomes the building.

## The decomposition (three needs, three different answers)

1. **The body's ORGANS die (model server).** The body must own this natively: spawn, health-poll, restart-with-backoff, circuit-break — inside ember-cli. #556's parent-liveness tether landed the first half (server dies with its parent); the restore half (CLI resurrects a dead server) must move from the watchdog into the CLI.
2. **The body crashes from its own defects.** Not a supervision need — a defect class. Render/feed errors must be contained, never process-fatal (#561 is the current instance).
3. **The body's own process dies** (kill, OOM, power). The only genuinely irreducible external need — a process cannot resurrect itself. The answer is a boring OS-native restart rule (Task Scheduler restart-on-failure or an equivalent 5-line supervisor), not a stateful polling daemon.

## Ladder

- r1: server supervision absorbed into ember-cli (restart-with-backoff + circuit breaker; planned-outage marker semantics move into the CLI/server contract).
- r2: crash-free bar — CLI survives its own render/feed exceptions with an in-pane error event, receipted.
- r3: external supervision reduced to one OS-native restart-on-failure registration for the CLI process itself.
- r4: liveness-watchdog.ps1 deleted from the process table permanently; restart-log lineage archived.

## Acceptance

- Kill the model server → CLI restores it natively, event rendered, receipt written.
- Kill the CLI process → OS rule restores it, receipt written on next boot.
- Zero hand-rolled watchdog processes running; window enumeration clean.

Constitution anchors: P-C (body co-equal, never lags the organism), §7 ladder (ember self-operates, audited), and the dependence-ratchet direction — external crutches must shrink measurably.

issues.title: stab480 v9 respec: optimizer hot-loop pace defect (k3 fire) - NS-on-GPU streaming, in-process commit read, grad-memmap persistence
issues.author: wordingone

clauses.text:
## Why (wall receipt — the k3 fire was a design defect, not instability)

The v8 stabilize leg (refs #480) was k3-killed at 2026-07-09T21:47Z: ≥54 min without banking a block whose v6 baseline is 11.7–13.5 min (79.7–83.0 s/step), GPU duty cycle 3.1% mean, trainer CPU-busy at ~178% of one core. Three live stack samples (leg-close receipt, refs #480) caught the optimizer step crawling through three CPU-bound phases. No NaN, no divergence, no CUDA error: the v7 commit-starvation cure (file-backed optimizer state) and the k3 pace requirement are in direct tension in the v8 design. This issue owns the v9 respec; no relaunch happens before this spec is frozen and implemented.

Class extraction (bottleneck ledger, refs #207): a memory-wall cure that relocates a hot-loop working set to slower storage must carry a pace receipt at the same rung — commit ceilings and step ceilings are ONE budget, not two.

## The three receipted defects

1. **Muon Newton–Schulz on disk-paged memory (dominant).** The inner optimizer's `_zeropower_via_newtonschulz5` executes on CPU over file-backed memmapped shadow parameters. For grown-width tensors (16384×32768) the NS matmul chain over paged memory converts an ~80 s step into a multi-thousand-second one.
2. **Commit-governor subprocess in the hot loop.** `_read_commit_gb` shells out to PowerShell (seconds per call). A live stack caught it firing INSIDE the step path — consistent with defect 3 re-arming the governed lazy-create branch every step.
3. **Front-load/zero_grad teardown race.** `zero_grad(set_to_none=True)` propagates to the inner optimizer whose params ARE the shadow params, tearing down the front-loaded `.grad.f32` memmap references each step — so step()'s lazy-create branch (and its per-parameter governor assert, defect 2) re-fires for every parameter on every step.

## Spec floor (v9 requirements; deviations need a dated comment here)

- R1: NS orthogonalization never runs over disk-paged memmaps. Either (a) stream each matmul-active shadow tensor to GPU for its NS chain (the GPU is idle during opt.step; VRAM cost is one tensor at a time, well inside the k1 band), or (b) keep the matmul-active (grown-width) tensors heap-resident, memmap residency retained for pure elementwise state (exp_avg / exp_avg_sq / momentum). Choice (a) preferred — it preserves the v8 commit profile (~47 GB, 46 GB under the v7 failure point).
- R2: the commit read becomes an in-process API call (Windows memory-status API via ctypes; microseconds). Governor semantics — phase-boundary asserts, ≥6 GB free-commit floor, abort-not-degrade — unchanged.
- R3: `.grad.f32` references persist across steps: zero_grad must zero-in-place or re-attach the persistent memmap, never tear down to None. The lazy-create branch may fire at most once per parameter per process lifetime; a receipt counter proves it (field `grad_lazy_creates`, must equal 0 after front-load).
- R4: in-run pace gate — the k3 enforcement moves inside the runner: if the first block since (re)launch has not banked within 2× the v6 baseline (≤27 min), the runner checkpoints what is consistent and aborts cleanly with a PACE_GATE marker. A coordinator-observed stall is the fallback, never the mechanism.
- R5: relaunch resumes from block-04 step-806 (unchanged, hash-verified); kill conditions k1/k2/k3 + CUBLAS-twice carry over verbatim; the existing prediction registers on refs #480 remain graded-as-closed for the v8 leg — the v9 leg gets a FRESH register filed before launch (register law: never retrofit).

## Acceptance

- AC1: implementation PR cites this issue (refs only), CPU-only unit evidence that R2/R3 hold (governor call count per step = 0 in steady state; grad_lazy_creates = 0).
- AC2: a pace smoke — one governed block on the real checkpoint — banks in ≤27 min with s/step receipted, VRAM inside k1, commit ≤ 58 GB.
- AC3: queue row added to refs #591 by dated comment; dispatch order after the services-restore row.

- **R3 false:** `_cpu_offload_init_with_frontloaded_grads` (cbase_grow_rung2_stabilize.py ~389–405) frontloads shadow grads once, but `timeshare_pretrain.py:603` calls `optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)` every step and `CPUOffloadOptimizer.zero_grad` (cpu_offload_adamw.py ~219–225) forwards `set_to_none=True` to the inner optimizer, tearing the shadow `.grad` memmaps down to `None` — the in-file comment says exactly this. Next step, the lazy-create branch (cpu_offload_adamw.py ~204–213) re-creates all `.grad.f32` memmaps through the governed wrapper. The M1 dominant term is structurally intact.
- **R2 absent:** `_read_commit_gb` (stabilize.py ~114–137) launches a PowerShell/Get-Counter subprocess; the governed wrapper calls it before every lazy grad create.
- **P2 falsifier blind:** the governed path emits nothing on success, so the prereg's "zero governor spawns in the log" prediction would pass vacuously while spawns occur — a falsifier-deleting instrument (same class as the #123 null-model rule).
- **R4 absent:** `_run_block` computes `wall_s` only after `run_v0_segment` returns (~1031–1050); no in-run pace gate can fire on a block that never returns — the exact v8 failure mode.
- **AC2 unsatisfied:** zero post-cure governed block receipts exist (the component benchmark was no-training).
- **Lineage:** the frozen resume point is **block-04 step-806** (comment 4929823617: banked blocks 1–4, losses 12.436/12.710/12.695/12.136); the withdrawn prereg silently rolled back to block-3.

## Frozen cure spec (implementation PR must satisfy ALL seven; each with a receipt in the PR)

1. **R2 — in-process commit read.** Replace the PowerShell subprocess in `_read_commit_gb` with an in-process API (e.g. `ctypes` `GlobalMemoryStatusEx` / `psutil.virtual_memory()`-equivalent commit counters), used by BOTH the printed stage markers and the governor decision (same-measurement invariant preserved). No subprocess anywhere in the step path.
2. **R3 — shadow-grad persistence.** `zero_grad` must never tear down the shadow `.grad.f32` memmaps: keep `set_to_none=True` semantics for the real (GPU) params, but the inner/shadow side either skips zeroing entirely (the step's `shadow_p.grad.copy_(g)` fully overwrites each step) or zeroes in place — design choice documented in-file. After the fix, lazy re-create is structurally unreachable in steady state.
3. **Observability counters + positive control.** `grad_lazy_creates` and `governor_reads` counters emitted on the SUCCESS path (per-block stage marker line), plus an executable positive-control test that forces one lazy create and asserts the counter fires. A prediction must be falsifiable by the log, not vacuously true.
4. **R4 — in-run pace gate.** A watchdog thread aborts the block cleanly (checkpoint + `PACE_GATE_ABORT` receipt) if the first block exceeds 27 min — abort-not-degrade, same shape as the commit governor.
5. **Two-consecutive-step test (executable, in the PR):** shadow-grad object identity stable across steps, `grad_lazy_creates == 0` after step 1, and the Newton–Schulz input tensors asserted heap-backed (not memmap views) — the v8 stack samples caught NS executing on file-backed shadows as the dominant crawl term.
6. **AC2 pace-smoke:** ONE governed real-checkpoint block banked at ≤27 min BEFORE the full leg is preregistered — the receipt #594's AC2 always required.
7. **Lineage:** resume from block-04 step-806 exactly (or a dated deviation entry if the checkpoint fails verification); leg = blocks 5–10.

issues.title: goal organ: update_goal(Complete) has no code-level completion-proof gate (floor clause 4 gap)
issues.author: wordingone

clauses.text:
## Gap

The goal-organ floor (docs/goal-mode-mechanism.md §4, GOAL.md §6) requires: "a completion audit
that must PROVE completion — an audit that merely fails to find remaining work is non-conforming
BY DEFINITION." Clause-by-clause audit (issue #642) found this clause has **zero code-level
enforcement**.

`update_goal(status: "Complete")` in `tools/ember-cli/src/tools/goal-tools.ts` accepts the
transition unconditionally whenever it is state-machine-legal (`Active -> Complete` and
`BudgetLimited -> Complete` are both legal per `core/goal-store.ts`'s `LEGAL_TRANSITIONS`). There
is no evidence parameter, no prior-audit-recorded check, and no verification of any kind — unlike
the sibling `Blocked` transition, which DOES have a code-enforced audit (`noteBlocked()` /
`BLOCKED_TURNS_THRESHOLD`, requiring the same blocker on 3+ consecutive turns before the store
will accept it).

The "must PROVE completion" requirement lives entirely as doctrine text injected into the model's
context (`core/goal-continuation-prompt.ts`'s `renderContinuationPrompt`'s COMPLETION AUDIT
paragraph). Nothing in the code path verifies the model actually performed that audit before
calling the tool — the mechanism is 100% prompt-trust for this clause, while the analogous
Blocked clause got a real code-level gate.

## Failing test (reproduces the gap)

`tools/ember-cli/src/core/goal-organ-floor-conformance-642.test.ts`, `CLAUSE 4` describe block —
committed `it.skip(...)` (kept green in CI; un-skip to reproduce). Raw failing output when
un-skipped, executed at `80458998a7f930ea1409259288d4606cb33f627a` on

288 |     const data = result.data as { ok: boolean; message?: string };

error: expect(received).toBe(expected)

✗ CLAUSE 4 — GAP: update_goal(Complete) has zero code-level completion-proof requirement > [GAP - tracked, see docs/goal-organ-floor-conformance-20260710.md row 4] update_goal(status:'Complete') should be REJECTED absent any recorded completion-audit evidence

structured per-requirement evidence list alongside `status: "Complete"` (mirroring Blocked's
`reason` requirement), and/or a minimum "audit tool calls since last continuation fire" counter
before Complete is accepted from a continuation-fired turn. Left to the implementing engineer —

Three specialist trainings remain (audio, reasoning, tool) plus future specialists and rungs; each will re-walk the same pipeline. The operator must eventually run this system alone. Bugs-as-we-go is disqualified as the process.

## 1. Rehearsal as an runtime-daemon feature (not seat discipline)
New command: `runtime-daemon rehearse <dispatch-manifest>` — automatically derives a minimal slice (subset records, few train steps, final checkpoint ON), runs the ENTIRE pipeline: admission -> data verify -> train -> checkpoint -> publish -> selectable-checkpoint claim -> (optional) restore probe, with the phase memory sampler mandatory, and emits a rehearsal receipt binding the exact source/manifest/contract hashes + measured whole-run host peak.
Admission rule (extends the already-ordered smoke-before-long-run gate): any dispatch above the step threshold REQUIRES a rehearsal receipt with matching bindings; episode simulated peak derives from the rehearsal's measured peak x margin, script-computed — never hand-estimated. This makes tonight's hard-won process the default path for audio/reasoning/tool with zero human judgment required.

## 2. Strict-gate census (each unaudited strict comparison is a latent run-killer)
Sweep runtime-daemon + tools/ember-restart-3b for every fail-closed strict comparison (exact field sets, exact string equality, exact hash sets). For each: (a) a build-time producer-consumer binding test in the #916 template (real producer output vs shared closed-world constant — drift fails the BUILD), or (b) a rehearsal-exercised proof it runs before any long spend. Deliverable: the census table in-repo with per-gate status; no gate left unclassified.

## 3. Operator-alone operability
- Every refusal receipt gains `next_action`: one plain-language sentence stating what to do (e.g. 'free host memory: close X or lower the cap; then rerun the same command').
- One entry point per capability: `runtime-daemon episode <capability>` chains preflight -> rehearsal (if no valid receipt) -> episode, refusing with plain receipts at each gate.
- A runbook doc generated from the actual receipt vocabulary (every refusal code -> meaning -> action), checked by a test that fails when a receipt code lacks a runbook entry.

Ordering: nothing here blocks the current episode dispatch. Item 1's admission half is already in flight; the rehearse command, census, and operability land immediately after, reviewed while training runs.
